correctness.rationale: Words are Euler trails on looped labeled multigraphs of positive edge count. The nonloop multiplicities split uniquely into an even part and a parity bit, and loops change no degree parity. A graph with c components contributes the top-interval partition Möbius sum, equal to one at c=1 and zero otherwise; the coefficient filter then selects zero or two odd vertices. Choosing the active alphabet and subtracting the q empty singleton terms proves the general formula. Separately authored direct multiplicity-category enumeration and integer cross-multiplication verified the quaternary rational expression and its eleven listed coefficients; replay: /workspace/branches/e9fead98-b918-4ce0-aecb-fb93e61ff240/record4_direct_categories.py. This is an exact q=4 algebra check, not an all-q experiment. In the limit, parity profiles have the same leading coefficient from the pole of order r at 1; the pole at −1 has order at most r−q. The incidence map over F2 has image all even vectors (edges from a fixed vertex give a basis). Counting weights zero and two gives the stated fraction; missing a cut edge forces a coordinate zero and costs one order in m. The full-support exception bound suffices also for proper connected active alphabets. For q≥4 an even weight-four obstruction exists; for q=2,3 none does. One representative per observation exactly attains the code size. Frozen verification files inspected, not executed.
